text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic receives chief prosecutor of International War Crimes Tribunal Louise Arbour, expresses hope that her activity will contribute to further promote cooperation and confidence.
- Serb parliament in Eastern Slavonia decides to submit request to Croatia and Yugoslavia to sign an inter-state agreement allowing dual citizenship.
- Yugoslav government adopts 1997 programme in which return to international organisations is a priority.

- No solution found yet for strike of department store Company RK Beograd a.d. which started on December 18. It covers 20 out of 46 stores and some 5,000 workers. Management schedules next meeting on January 28.

- Acting director of Radio Television Kragujevac Vidosav Stevanovic to hold talks in Belgrade with director of Radio TV Serbia Dragoljub Milanovic on dispute over Kragujevac TV which has provoked several days of protests in that town.
- Belgrade University Rector Dragutin Velickovic says he will resign as soon as students return to regular classes.

- Independent trade union of city transport company GSP gives up strike after reaching partial agreement with city authorities to increase price of labour by about 10 percent and give advance pay by end of January.
NASA BORBA

- Open letter of group of prominent economic experts on measures for getting Yugoslavia out of economic crisis which include normalisation of relations with IMF, stable economic and legal regulations, convertible dinar and stable exchange rate.
- Teachers of several Belgrade schools on strike over unpaid wages and dissatisfaction with new labour relations law.
- Pan-Serb two-day congress opening in Pristina Saturday to discuss Serb national interests, and Serb-Albanian relations.

- Ex-Yugoslavia succession talks end in Brussels without any progress. International negotiator Sir Arthur Watts proposes that sides prepare their list of assets to be shared out for next round of talks tentatively scheduled for mid-February.
- Main board of Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) confirms decision on ousting of Belgrade mayor Nebojsa Covic and head of Nis Socialists Mile Ilic from the party.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Protesters block traffic in Kraljevo and on Ibar highway. Several people injured in clash with police after protesters tried to break through police cordon. Opposition coalition attempts to blockade highways into Nis and Krusevac fail.

- Belgrade city election commission's call for the exclusion of some 60 judges would mean no decision could be made on complaints over elections lodged by Zajedno coalition, Socialist Party of Serbia and Serbian Radical Party until it is decided who will rule on them, says Belgrade District Court judge Miroslav Todorovic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Serbia's shipyards plan income of $70 million from exports in 1997. Main obstacle lack of bank guarantees and credits.
